attache.introTexte: Twenty questions about what you feel for your partner, and about what keeps you with them. The two are measured separately, because you can perfectly well score high on both.
attache.resultatLibelle: What binds you, in two measures
attache.q1: When your partner tells you about something, how do you listen?
attache.q1a: I want to hear the rest, I ask questions.
attache.q1b: I listen, without necessarily following up.
attache.q1c: With one ear, I've got the general idea already.
attache.q1d: Mostly I wait for it to be over.
attache.q2: You picture your life without this person. What comes first:
attache.q2a: The emptiness: the flat, the evenings, the silence.
attache.q2b: The logistics: where I'd go, how we'd split everything.
attache.q2c: A mix of relief and nerves.
attache.q3: If you met this person today, for the first time:
attache.q4: What you'd lose by leaving, apart from the person:
attache.q4a: A lot: the home, the friends, the routines, a whole life.
attache.q5: Someone speaks well of your partner to you:
attache.q5a: It makes me happy, and I add to it.
attache.q5c: It doesn't do much for me.
attache.q6: When the thought of a break-up crosses your mind:
attache.q6a: I push it away straight away.
attache.q6b: It tightens my chest, then I move on.
attache.q6c: I think about it calmly, now and then.
attache.q6d: I think about it often, without it scaring me.
attache.q7: Physical desire, as things stand today:
attache.q7a: It's there, and not only on a Saturday night.
attache.q7b: Less often than before, but it's there.
attache.q7c: Rare, and more out of habit.
attache.q8: The years spent together, when you start asking yourself questions:
attache.q8a: They're an argument for staying, I tell myself that often.
attache.q8b: I think about them now and then.
attache.q9: When your partner comes home in the evening:
attache.q9a: I'm glad to see them, clearly.
attache.q9c: It doesn't do anything in particular to me.
attache.q10: Picturing yourself on your own, six months from now:
attache.q10c: It doesn't thrill me, but I'd be fine.
attache.q10d: It doesn't bother me at all.
attache.q11: Their plans, what's keeping them busy right now, what's on their mind:
attache.q11a: I know about it, and it interests me.
attache.q11d: I haven't asked myself that in a long time.
attache.q12: How they'd react if you left:
attache.q12a: I think about it, and it's one of the things holding me back.
attache.q12b: I think about it, without it deciding everything.
attache.q12d: That isn't what holds me back.
attache.q13: You get some good news. You tell them:
attache.q14: The settled everyday, the habits you've built together:
attache.q14a: It's comfortable, and I don't want it to change.
attache.q14b: It's comfortable, but I could do without it.
attache.q14d: I'd just as soon it changed.
attache.q15: A weekend just the two of you, nothing you have to do:
attache.q15a: I want that, and I'm usually the one who suggests it.
attache.q15b: I want that if it's well planned.
attache.q16: When they're away for a few days, what you miss:
attache.q16a: Having someone in the flat in the evening.
attache.q16b: A bit of both: the person and the presence.
attache.q16c: The person themselves, their stories, the way they are.
attache.q17: One quality of this person, right now:
attache.q17c: I have to think about it for a while.
attache.q18: Your circle, your friends, both families:
attache.q18a: It's all mixed together, it would count enormously in a decision.
attache.q19a: I want it sorted out, and quickly.
attache.q19b: I wait for it to settle, then we talk.
attache.q19c: I let it drag, I don't much mind.
attache.q19d: Part of me is almost relieved.
attache.q20: If you were certain you'd meet someone good within the year:
attache.q20a: It would change nothing, I'd stay.
attache.q20b: It would make me think for a while, then I'd stay.
attache.q20c: It would make me seriously hesitate.
attache.p_deux_t: Love, and a bond that holds
attache.p_deux_d: Both of your measures are high, and that's the most common result among couples who are doing well. You want this person, they still interest you, and at the same time your life is bound up with theirs to the point where losing them would cost you a lot. The two don't cancel each other out. Attachment isn't the opposite of love, it's what gets built when you share years, a home, habits and the same people. A couple with one and not the other would be either a passion with no roots, or a flatshare.
attache.p_deux_a: Nothing to repair here. The one thing to keep an eye on is the love bar, because that's the one you maintain: it drops quietly the day you stop asking each other questions. Ask one now and then, about what they'd like to do with the next five years, for instance.
attache.p_amour_d: The love side comes out clearly on top. You stay for the person, not for what you'd lose by leaving: you'd manage on your own, the silence in the flat doesn't scare you, and you don't need to remind yourself of the years behind you to justify staying. It's the calmest of the five results, and one of the least common, because it takes either a relationship that's still young, or someone who has kept enough of a life of their own.
attache.p_amour_a: This position makes things simple: a decision taken without fear of the void is nearly always the right one. The one case to watch is your partner being on the attachment side instead. That imbalance always shows up in the end. Have them take the test on their side and compare the two bars rather than the verdicts.
attache.p_attachement_d: The gap is clear, and it's probably what you suspected when you landed on this page. What keeps you in this relationship comes mostly down to what you'd lose by leaving: the silence in the flat, the years already spent, the shared friends, the face they'd make. All of that is real and genuinely counts, nobody leaves someone without weighing it. Only, none of those arguments is about the person themselves, and that's where it plays out.
attache.p_attachement_a: An exercise that helps, done honestly: write down everything that holds you here, then cross out whatever is about your own comfort rather than about your partner. What's left is the answer. If the page ends up blank, it doesn't mean you have to leave tomorrow morning, it means there's a conversation to have, and it has already waited long enough.
attache.p_melange_t: A bit of both, in nearly equal parts
attache.p_melange_d: The two measures are level, with neither crushing the other, and neither of them is very high. This is the result of the flat stretches: the relationship holds, the affection is there, but the momentum is idling and what keeps you doesn't look like a prison either. Plenty of couples go through this after a birth, a move, a hard year at work. It describes a moment, not necessarily the bottom of your relationship.
attache.p_melange_a: Don't settle anything just yet: at this level, the result moves a lot from one month to the next. Look instead at what has changed in the past six months, outside the relationship. And take the test again in a few weeks: if the love bar climbs back, it was tiredness; if it drops further, it was something else.
attache.p_fini_d: Both bars are low, and it's the only result that leaves little room for doubt. You don't particularly want this person any more, and you don't dread what would come next either. In other words, not much is keeping you. Most people who get this result already knew, and mostly came to hear it said out loud.
attache.p_fini_a: You don't need a spectacular reason to leave, or to wait for the argument that would justify everything. What helps at this stage is setting a date for the conversation instead of waiting for the right moment, because it isn't coming. And if a doubt remains, it's usually less about the relationship than about what follows it.
